newsitem.title: USA: Wheatland, Calif., defaults on bonds - official.
newsitem.headline: Wheatland, Calif., defaults on bonds - official.

text.p: The city of Wheatland in northern California defaulted Friday on its bond payments for the first time, the city administrator said.

"We did not make the payments," said Wheatland Administrator Clay Castleberry. "The (bond) reserves were almost exhausted, leaving not enough money to make the scheduled payments. I'm disappointed for the city."
Wheatland's $2.1 million of Mello-Roos bonds were issued in 1990 to pay for sewer and highway improvements in areas planned for development of hundreds of housing units.
The Wheatland development has been marred by financial problems due to delinquencies by major property owners. Last November, Wheatland was forced to draw down on bond reserves to pay investors.
Castleberry said the city would continue to pursue foreclosure actions against delinquent property owners.
In August, the city sent notices to bondholders warning of the likelihood of a default on the Mello-Roos bond payments on November 1.
Castleberry said he believed the default was the first ever by the small city.

The Wheatland bond issue had been the subject of a Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry. But, in late May, the SEC told the city it was dropping its probe. The SEC is still investigating the deal's underwriter, San Francisco-based First California Capital Markets Group Inc.
